decisions.reason: As a closely related product line with its own page, it likely meets at least near-term aspirations well enough for a medium-sized engineering firm with some slack to keep learning and selling it.
Although only briefly presented, it supports the firm's strategic push toward automation, so boundedly rational management would likely retain it while results are still emerging.

This is close to the core offer but has weaker visible commitment than products with dedicated pages, so it faces some risk if early demand falls short of aspiration, yet is still more likely to be retained for now.
A dedicated-page product line that fits existing formwork capabilities is likely to stay because it uses established resources and does not yet justify problemistic withdrawal.

Its own-page presentation suggests a meaningful commercial commitment, and its close fit with the installed product architecture makes continuation the more likely choice under uncertain early performance.

Because it is only mentioned and appears to overlap with adjacent magnetic formwork offerings, it has the highest pruning risk if it underperforms aspiration levels, but the firm would still probably keep it one more year.
